sections.html:
In Yadkinville, the register of deeds is the keeper of land records for the whole county, including deeds, deeds of trust and maps. Anyone may inspect them. Staff also certify copies of birth, death and marriage certificates, issues marriage licenses and swears in notaries.

Until the deed is on the books, a sale is not fully protected. An unregistered conveyance loses to lien creditors and later buyers who paid value, and whoever registers first generally ranks first.

Electronic recording is encouraged for every document. Appointments for marriage licenses and notary oaths go through 336-849-7904. Voters elect the register, and the deed excise tax is paid at this same counter, so a seller's money and the buyer's paperwork meet here.

sections.h2: How a deed gets recorded after a sale
sections.html:
In most sales the attorney or title company sends the deed in electronically from the closing table. The register accepts every document type except maps by e-recording. A firm that wants to submit must go through Simplifile, CSC or ePN and complete a submitter agreement that the provider passes to the county.

The county's tax office points owners to an attorney for deed work. As a result, a seller in Yadkinville, Jonesville, East Bend or anywhere between rarely visits the recording desk personally.

  • Ask if your closing firm already has an e-recording agreement here.
  • Learn who is writing the check for the excise tax. The seller owes it.
  • Keep the recording confirmation as proof of the date and time of registration.
  • Bringing paper instead? Phone the office before you drive over.

The fee schedule is the same in every North Carolina county. It is complete and exclusive, and payment is due up front.

Charges that apply to a Yadkin County house sale
DocumentAmount
Deed, first 15 pages$26.00
Mortgage, first 35 pages$64.00
Overflow pages on either$4.00 each
Paying off a mortgage (satisfaction)Free
Certified copy of a recorded deed$5.00 plus $2.00 per added page
Nonstandard document$25.00 added

Tally the pages of the deed plus exhibits ahead of time. The $4.00 charge begins on the sixteenth page of a general instrument.

The transferring owner pays this tax. The rate is one dollar per five hundred dollars of value, due at the register's counter ahead of the filing.

The proceeds are split evenly: the county keeps half, and the other half is sent to the state each month, minus up to 2 percent the county may hold back. The settlement statement shows the dollar amount for your sale price.

If a house passes as a gift or between relatives, ask the office how a stated value is treated before anyone signs.

sections.h2: Tax office versus Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Think of them as two counters with different jobs. The Yadkin County Tax Department in Yadkinville lists and bills property, takes exemption applications and keeps the parcel maps. The register of deeds only records the paper. A 2027 revaluation is underway at the tax office.

Billing and payment questions go to the tax office at 336-849-7903. That office gives a 2 percent discount for August payment and bills a solid waste fee of $76.00 per household ($38.00 with the elderly exemption). Taxes are due September 1, with interest beginning January 6.

The recording desk takes more than deeds. Options, leases beyond three years and rights of first refusal must be registered before they bind a later buyer. A seller who gave a buyer an option months ago should check that it was recorded, since an unrecorded one may not hold up against a new purchaser.

A seller-financed sale is the other case worth knowing. North Carolina's Chapter 47H covers a contract for deed with five or more payments, where the seller keeps title. Written and acknowledged terms are required, the buyer gets a three-business-day cancellation window, and the seller records the contract or a memorandum within five business days. A forfeiture notice has to allow at least 30 days to cure (Chapter 47H).

  • Satisfactions of a deed of trust record for no fee, so paying off a mortgage costs nothing at this office.
  • For a parcel split between counties, the excise tax goes to the county holding the greater value.
  • An estate sale may require a small estate affidavit to list each tract the decedent owned.

sections.h2: Sales of inherited and older houses
sections.html:
Of Yadkin County's 17,697 housing units, owners occupy 76.9 percent, and plenty of sales involve inherited or aging houses. Builders pulled only 116 permits in 2025, so resale homes dominate. An older house often has a longer chain of deeds, and a buyer's title examiner will read every link, from the first conveyance to your own vesting deed.

When an estate owns the house, ask the clerk of superior court who may sign the deed. The register takes it once it is signed and acknowledged, yet staff will not rule on the signer's authority.

sections.h2: If the owner has a tax lien
sections.html:
An owner facing a tax lien can look at the county's Tax Foreclosure Sales page to see how auctions are listed. Redemption remains possible before a sale is confirmed.

Any lien will turn up in the buyer's title exam. Clear it before you list, because a late discovery can delay closing or shrink your proceeds. Ask the tax office for a payoff figure that includes the solid waste fee, and give it to the closing attorney.

You will rarely do this yourself, but it helps to know what your closing firm needs. Yadkin County takes every document type except maps by e-recording, and the firm must work through Simplifile, CSC or ePN.

  1. The firm picks one of the three providers.
  2. It completes a submitter agreement, which the provider passes to the county.
  3. It sends the signed deed and the deed of trust electronically.
  4. It keeps the confirmation showing the date and time of recording.

If your attorney does not already have an agreement with Yadkin County, ask whether paper recording will be used and how long the office will need. A plat or map always goes in on paper.

sections.h2: Questions to ask your closing attorney
sections.html:
A short conversation with your attorney saves surprises at the register's counter. Ask who is responsible for the recording fee, whether any exhibits will push the deed past 15 pages, and whether the deed of trust for the buyer's loan will be filed the same day. Ask too whether an old option or lease in your chain of title has been recorded, and whether any seller-financed terms would fall under Chapter 47H.

If you live outside Yadkin County while the house is in it, the attorney can handle everything by e-recording, and you will only need to sign.

1. Learn whether your attorney will record electronically or on paper.
  2. Estimate the recording fee from the page count of the deed and exhibits.
  3. Decide who writes the excise tax check.
  4. Verify a satisfaction is on record for any mortgage you paid off.
  5. File the recording confirmation with your closing papers.

A cash sale skips the buyer's lender and its deed of trust, so the packet is smaller, but the deed and the excise tax are still recorded in the same way. Ask your attorney for the recording date and time, because that timestamp, not the signing date, fixes who ranks first.

faqs.q: Does Yadkin County charge a transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The seller owes a deed excise tax, paid to the register at filing. The rate is one dollar for each five hundred dollars of value.

faqs.q: Can a Yadkin County deed be recorded electronically?
faqs.a: Yes, any document except a map. The attorney or title company must first sign a submitter agreement through Simplifile, CSC or ePN. For paper filings, phone 336-849-7904.

faqs.q: Does it cost anything to record a satisfaction of a mortgage?
faqs.a: No. State law sets no charge for a satisfaction, so the payoff paperwork is free to file.

faqs.q: How long does a buyer under a contract for deed have to cancel?
faqs.a: Through midnight of the third business day. After that, the seller has a five-business-day window to record.

faqs.q: Is a Yadkin County revaluation coming?
faqs.a: Yes, a 2027 revaluation is underway. Counties must reappraise all real estate on an eight-year cycle at the longest.
